title: Dark Matter
body:
**Dark matter** is mass that gravitates and emits no light. It was inferred from its gravity,
since it emits nothing to observe directly, and the inference rests on several independent
measurements agreeing.

**Galactic rotation curves.** Orbital speed in a galaxy should fall beyond the visible mass, in
the way the outer planets orbit more slowly than the inner ones. Measured speeds stay flat far
past the stars, which requires mass extending well beyond the light. See [[Milky Way]].

**Cluster dynamics.** Galaxies within a cluster move too fast for the visible mass to hold them
together, which Zwicky noticed in the 1930s. The cluster should have dispersed long ago.

**Gravitational lensing.** Mass bends light passing near it, so a cluster distorts the images
of galaxies behind it, and the distortion measures the mass. The measured mass exceeds the
visible mass by roughly a factor of five, and lensing maps show it distributed differently from
the galaxies.

**Structure formation.** Ordinary matter alone cannot clump fast enough after the
[[Cosmic Microwave Background]] to produce the galaxies observed. Additional
gravitating matter is required for the timeline to work.

The four measurements are independent and agree on the amount, which is what makes the
conclusion hard to avoid. Its composition is unknown, and the candidates are non-baryonic
particles that interact through gravity and not through light. Modifying gravity is the
alternative and struggles to fit all four lines at once.

Ordinary matter is roughly 5% of the universe's content, dark matter about 27%, and dark
energy, which drives the accelerating expansion in [[Hubble's Law]], the remaining 68%.
